attacks.claim: The plan asserts that extra sizes and formats of wire photos (AP, Reuters) are licensed, but the only support is a photo-desk confirmation reference. No licence clause or scope of reviewed agreements is cited. Wire licences often restrict modification and redistribution, so new derivatives served under new keys need verification against the actual contract terms before crossing.
attacks.evidence: Wire images (AP, Reuters) are already resized for display. Extra sizes and formats of the same licensed image for the same display use are covered by the current licences (photo desk confirmation on WEB-778, Oct 19).

attacks.claim: The takedown purge is not shown to be complete or race-safe. Prefix deletion can run while make_responsive_set is still writing, which could recreate derivative keys after a takedown purge. The only test covers a fully written set, and the plan says nothing about purging external copies, audit retention, or legal hold.
attacks.evidence: It is extended to delete every key under the image's `<id>-` prefix and invalidate `/media/YYYY/MM/<id>-*`. Test: purge an image with a full responsive set; assert zero remaining keys and one wildcard invalidation.

attacks.claim: The has_responsive_set flag is set by the task, but the plan does not say it is set only after every derivative upload succeeds. It also does not define cleanup of partial output or idempotent retry for a half-written set. A partial write could leave the flag true with missing formats, or false with orphaned keys.
attacks.evidence: `` is rendered only when `image.has_responsive_set` is true (set by the task). ... 3 retries, then alert to #web-alerts; the page keeps the plain ``. ABSENT: atomicity of flag-setting relative to S3 writes, and cleanup of partial output on retry.

attacks.claim: A browser that supports AVIF or WebP selects that <source> and does not fall back to the JPEG if the object returns a 4xx or 5xx. Monitoring covers only 4xx on derivative paths, with no 5xx alert and no ratio of <picture> renders to successful derivative fetches, so a broken format path could hurt LCP on 62% mobile traffic before the 100% step.
attacks.evidence: Browsers without AVIF take WebP; browsers with neither take JPEG (standard `<picture>` fallback). ... Monitoring: RUM p75 LCP/CLS per group; CloudFront 4xx rate on `*.avif` / `*.webp`

attacks.claim: The LCP success case rests on prototype numbers measured with the 800 px AVIF candidate. The sizes attribute at 720 CSS px on a high-DPR device selects a larger candidate (up to 1600 px for AVIF/WebP), so the bytes and LCP measured do not represent the selection path that devices will actually take.
attacks.evidence: 800 px AVIF median 61 KB, WebP 88 KB. WebPageTest (Moto G Power, 4G, 3 runs per article): p75 LCP 3.9 s → 2.6 s. ... `sizes="(max-width: 720px) 100vw, 720px"`

attacks.claim: The claim that publishing is 'never delayed' rests only on a separate low-priority queue. The plan does not say whether the backfill uses dedicated worker processes, so the same CPU and memory may serve publishing. No memory or CPU ceiling is stated for libvips decoding 40-megapixel originals.
attacks.evidence: Two existing worker nodes × 4 workers ≈ 9.7 h, run over two nights (01:00–06:00) on a separate low-priority Celery queue, so publishing tasks are never delayed.

attacks.claim: The candidate sets are not fully specified across formats. JPEG is listed at 480/800/1200 while AVIF and WebP go to 1600, and the plan does not state whether the existing 1600 JPEG is included in the srcset.
attacks.evidence: an `` with the JPEG `srcset`; `src` is the existing 1600 px JPEG. ... JPEG at 480/800/1200 px and AVIF (q 50) and WebP (q 75) at 480/800/1200/1600 px

attacks.claim: Image parsing runs libvips 8.14 on staff-uploaded files with no worker sandboxing stated. Patching depends on unattended-upgrades for the pinned version, which is not verified. HEIC decoding dependencies are not discussed, though validation and VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED reduce the risk.
attacks.evidence: libvips 8.14 from the Debian 12 package (LGPL-2.1, dynamically linked; security updates via unattended-upgrades) ... workers run with `VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED=1`.

attacks.claim: Metadata stripping is tested only with one fixture carrying GPS, XMP and IPTC. HEIC inputs, which are the most likely to carry embedded location data, are not explicitly covered by the test.
attacks.evidence: New test: build every derivative from a fixture carrying GPS EXIF, XMP and IPTC; assert none of it survives in any output.

attacks.claim: No visual quality comparison is planned for AVIF q50 and WebP q75 on the 720 px column, so the reader-facing quality outcome is asserted rather than measured.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no visual quality comparison or reader-facing metric in section 8; only CrUX p75 mobile LCP and p75 CLS targets.

attacks.claim: The egress saving (~$1,000/month) is the main business-case figure, but it is projected from prototype byte savings applied to September's mix without hit-rate or format-mix data. It is labelled an estimate, so the case for the 100% step is weaker than the headline implies.
attacks.evidence: projected ~9 TB by applying the prototype's byte savings to September's traffic mix, ≈ $1,000/month less. This is an estimate
